messages:
alisa: Quick follow-up from the weight-loading RFC thread — proposing a tiny refactor to the loader boundary to make warmup+shard headers first-class and avoid special-casing safetensors vs tar shards.

alisa: Problem we saw in staging: first request to a new shard pays ~130ms to read a few small header blocks + mmap setup, which cascades to many concurrent requests and spikes tail latency.

tom: Yep. Replaying: root causes were (1) we read whole manifest + checksum sync on open, (2) some hosts did non-blocking mmap which triggered page faults later, (3) tiny tensors (pos emb) were in remote shard and forced a large range read.

rahul: +1 to separating “metadata header” read from content open. If WeightSource exposes stat()/headers() we can warm those on scheduler thread before handing to runtime.

maria: Suggest API sketch (pseudo):
```
interface WeightSource {
  stat(): Promise<{size: number, sha256?: string, headers?: string[]}>
  open(range?: {start:number, end:number}): AsyncIterator<Uint8Array> // streaming body
  warmup(prefixes: string[]): Promise<void> // best-effort prefetch / advice
}
```
This keeps callers unaware of safetensors vs checkpoint tar; they just call headers() then warmup for small prefixes.

tom: Tradeoffs:
- pro: we can prefix-warm tiny tensors (emb, ln) synchronously before first token -> big p50 improvement.
- con: extra roundtrip for small local files if caller always calls stat(), but stat can be cached per-model-version.

rahul: Also need to clarify who verifies checksums. Two options: verify during stat() (fail fast) or verify lazily during background warmup and mark source unhealthy if mismatch. I prefer verify-in-stat for enterprise/private deployments; hosted can opt for lazy verify to speed startup.

alisa: Agreed. Add config flag: verifyOnStat: boolean on WeightSourceFactory. Default true for Private, false for Hosted accelerated path.

maria: Implementation details: for mmap-backed sources we should:
- read the safetensors header into a small buffer (<= 8KB)
- parse tensor offsets to build a per-tensor offset table (store in metadata cache)
- for warmup, issue ranged reads for small tensors and call madvise(MADV_WILLNEED) for large contiguous regions
- for quantized layouts ensure 16-byte alignment; use posix_memalign if we need pinned buffers

tom: Note on hugepages: 2MB pages help reduce TLB pressure for 50B params but complicate partial mappings. We should keep hugepage allocation as an opt-in allocation pool for big-model dedicated nodes, not default.

infra-bot: deploy-log: weight-loader-refactor branch built and ran unit tests (12s).

rahul: Also, for sharded objects we should prefer a small shard-local header file ("shardname.header.json") that contains a compact index (tensor->offset,len, type, qtype). Pros: listing one small file is cheap and predictable. Cons: more files to manage, but we already upload manifests.

maria: Alternative is embed the header at start of the shard file with a 32-bit magic and footer pointing to header. That keeps single file per shard but requires reading footer (last 4KB) to find header offset which is an extra seek. For S3 this costs another range read. I prefer shard-local .header for faster first-byte.

tom: For streaming backends (http-range) we should ensure open(range) is an async stream of chunks so runtime can start piping into GPU copy threads as bytes arrive. Good to keep split: metadata first, then stream content.

alisa: Long-term refactor idea: introduce WeightSourceFactory that returns a WeightSource plus a WarmupPlan. WarmupPlan describes small prefixes to prefetch with priority. Scheduler can aggregate warmup plans across in-flight requests to dedupe.

rahul: Example WarmupPlan: ["/model/embeddings/0:0-65535","/model/ln1:0-4096"], and we dedupe by URL+range. Saves a lot on concurrent cold-starts.

maria: Metrics to add: cold_open_latency(p50/p95), warmup_hit_rate, deduped_warm_requests, header_parse_time. We should record whether warmup used madvise or ranged read.

tom: Migration plan:
1) implement header files and stat()/headers() in WeightSource for safetensors + tar shards.
2) add warmup() call at model load path and in runtime for canary first requests.
3) opt-in verifyOnStat flag per deployment type.
4) after 2 weeks of canary, flip hosted default to warm-first.

alisa: Sounds good. Any objections or further concerns about API surface?

rahul: One more: add an idempotent cancel handle for warmup so scheduler can cancel low-priority warmups if backpressure.

maria: +1. Also document expected semantics: warmup best-effort, may not guarantee page residency.

tom: I'll draft a short follow-up RFC PR with the interface and a tiny benchmark showing cold p50 -> 6ms from 12ms for small-chat models.

alisa: Thanks all — leaving action items in RFC PR. :thumbsup:
